gap: No result ChatGPT got states that The Center Column measured the Peak Design Travel Tripod Carbon at 349 Nm/rad yaw (twist) stiffness and 1007.8 Nm/rad pitch, against 184 and 618 Nm/rad for the Manfrotto Befree Advanced. That makes the Peak Design about 1.9× stiffer in twist, and its ranking stiffness is 518 against 284 for the Befree.
standout_why: Finding the Universe, which ChatGPT cited and which was updated 2026-11-08, gives only maker specs, with a note that they were 'locked in July 2026'. Its only judgements are the author's own impressions ('holds my R5 with the 100-400mm attached without complaint'), with no stiffness, damping or measured weight. Digital Camera World, ChatGPT's other cited page, would not load for me: WebFetch returned 85 characters, so I could not check it. Its related reviews that turned up in searches describe stability in words, not stiffness figures. TechGearLab and On Landscape, which ChatGPT did not get, also hold no stiffness figures. On Landscape says it relied on The Center Column for stiffness data. I did not open the DPReview 2020 test, the PhotoWorkout page or the other uncited pages.
decides: For a DSLR with a heavy zoom, the measured stiffness favours the Peak Design over the Befree Advanced. Even the aluminium Peak Design (456) beats the Befree (284) on ranking stiffness, so the figures argue against ChatGPT's 'Befree Advanced Carbon for most DSLR users' if a heavy lens is the concern. Two caveats: The Center Column tested an aluminium twist-lock Befree Advanced (it posted around 2020–21), not the current AS lever-lock or carbon versions ChatGPT showed, and GearLab's hands-on stability score (how sharp shots came out in sideways-push and wind tests) puts the Befree Advanced slightly ahead, at 7.4 against 7.0. The SIRUI Traveler 5C, which Dealectric lists, scored GearLab's lowest stability in this group (5.0/10, 'quite wobly when fully extended'). That argues against it as a DSLR pick despite its 1.9 lb measured weight.
candidates: Peak Design Travel Tripod Carbon Fiber

findings.label: Stiffness, pitch and yaw (The Center Column)
findings.source_title: Peak Design Travel Tripod Review – The Center Column
findings.note: Measured with a 3/8" adapter and no head. A heavy weight is set swinging; the swing frequency gives stiffness and how fast it dies out gives damping (method page: thecentercolumn.com/testing-tripod-stiffness-and-damping-at-the-center-column/). The tester bought this tripod through Kickstarter and says Peak Design paid him for earlier prototype testing but not for this review. The page has no date; its images are dated Feb 2020.

findings.label: Damping, measured weight, folded volume (The Center Column)
findings.value: Damping 0.213 Js/rad pitch, 0.143 Js/rad yaw; 2.39 lb (1.083 kg) without head; 1.2 L folded; 50.5 in max height with the centre column down
findings.source_title: Peak Design Travel Tripod Review – The Center Column
findings.note: The folded length is given as 14.2 in in the spec table but '15 inches' in the text, so I left it out.

findings.label: Stiffness, pitch and yaw (The Center Column)
findings.source_title: Manfrotto Befree Advanced Test Results – The Center Column
findings.note: The page lists aluminium legs and twist locks, so this is not the AS lever-lock or carbon version ChatGPT showed. Yaw ratio against the Peak Design Carbon: 349/184 = 1.90×.

findings.label: Damping, measured weight, folded size (The Center Column)
findings.value: Damping 0.426 Js/rad pitch, 0.196 Js/rad yaw; 2.56 lb (1.162 kg), apparently without head; 17.2 in folded; 2.2 L; 46.1 in max height with the centre column down
findings.source_title: Manfrotto Befree Advanced Test Results – The Center Column
findings.note: The Befree damps more than the Peak Design in both axes (0.426 vs 0.213 pitch). The site gives damping errors as an assumed 10%.

findings.label: Travel tripod ranking stiffness (The Center Column)
findings.value: PD Travel Tripod Carbon 518.0; PD Aluminum 456.0; Manfrotto BeFree Advanced 284.0; Gitzo GT1545T 792.0; RRS TFC-14 1071.0
findings.source_title: Travel Tripod Rankings – The Center Column
findings.note: The ranking stiffness is the harmonic mean of pitch and yaw at full height. Check: 2/(1/1007.8 + 1/349) = 518.5 and 2/(1/618 + 1/184) = 283.6, matching the table. Ranking score = stiffness × height^1.25 ÷ weight. The prices in the table ($350 PD Aluminum, $190 Befree) are old, so I did not use them. Newest archive entry on the page is Feb 2021.

findings.label: Stability score out of 10 (GearLab hands-on tests)
findings.value: Manfrotto Befree Advanced 7.4; Peak Design Travel 7.0; SIRUI Traveler 5C 5.0
findings.note: Method: a few pounds of sideways pressure on flat and uneven ground, 1-second exposures in wind at three heights, and about 20-second night exposures. The page does not say which Befree or Peak Design versions were tested.

findings.label: Measured weight (GearLab)
findings.value: Manfrotto Befree Advanced 3.51 lb; Peak Design Travel 3.68 lb; SIRUI Traveler 5C 1.9 lb
findings.note: The page does not say which material versions were weighed or what was included.

findings.label: GearLab review scores and verdict
findings.value: Overall 74 (#10 of 17); Stability 5.0/10; Portability 9.4/10; measured 1.9 lb; 13 in folded; 8.8 lb load
findings.source_title: SIRUI Lightweight Carbon Fiber Traveler 5C Review – TechGearLab (Zach Lovell, 2026-08-20)
findings.note: Zach Lovell: the centre column 'wasn't very confidence-inspiring in the wind' and is 'quite wobly when fully extended'.
